question: A product is sold for ₹ 3,400 after a 15% discount. What was the original marked price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given Discount = 15%

⇒ Selling Price = 100% − 15% = 85% of Marked Price

⇒ 85% = ₹ 3,400

⇒ 100% = (3400 ÷ 85) × 100 = ₹ 4,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 4,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹ 3,400

Discount = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Discount%]

 
 
 SP = ₹ 3,400 (85%)
 
 15%
 

 Discount
 

 MP = 100%

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = (3400 × 100) ÷ (100 − 15)

⇒ MP = (3400 × 100) ÷ 85

⇒ MP = 40 × 100

⇒ MP = ₹ 4,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 4,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is an allowance given to the buyer and is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article, not on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by: [a + b − (a × b)÷100]%.

Relationship Between CP, MP, Profit% and Discount%

A highly useful direct ratio relation is: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
